tour.name: Giverny & Rouen Private Day Trip from Paris: Monet's House, Garden & Water Lilies
tour.subtitle: A private day in the footsteps of the Impressionists with a licensed guide and car: Claude Monet's house and garden at Giverny with its water lily pond and Japanese bridge, lunch in the village, and the old city of Rouen, its cathedral painted by Monet and the square where Joan of Arc died.

tour.overview:
In 1883 Claude Monet saw the village of Giverny from a train window and decided to live there. For 43 years, until his death in 1926, he turned the land around his pink house into a work of art: a flower garden in front and, across the road, a pond he dug and planted with water lilies, crossed by a Japanese bridge. The garden became his subject, and the Water Lilies paintings that fill the Orangerie in Paris were born here. Downstream on the Seine, Rouen, the old capital of Normandy, inspired another famous series: thirty views of its cathedral at different times of day.

This private day takes you to both, with a licensed guide and a car. You visit Monet's house and gardens in the morning, when the light is soft and the paths are quiet, have lunch in the village, and spend the afternoon in Rouen, among its Gothic churches and half-timbered houses, where Joan of Arc was tried and burned.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 9 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Paris
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy; about 4 km on garden paths and old-town streets

WHAT YOU SEE
• Monet's house: the studio-salon, the yellow dining room and the kitchen.
• The Clos Normand flower garden.
• The Water Garden, the water lily pond and the Japanese bridge.
• Rouen Cathedral.
• The Gros-Horloge and the old town.
• The Old Market Square and the church of Joan of Arc.

WHY THIS WORKS
We arrive in Giverny at opening time, before the gardens fill with coach groups, and give Rouen a full afternoon instead of the quick stop most tours make.

WHO IT SUITS
Art and garden lovers, photographers and anyone who loves Impressionism.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer palaces, choose our Versailles tour; for a combination of Normandy's coast and abbey, choose Mont-Saint-Michel.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Monet's house and gardens are open only from about 1 April to 1 November. The gardens change every few weeks: tulips in April, irises in May, roses in June, water lilies from June to September and dahlias in autumn.

days.name: Monet's house and gardens at Giverny, lunch in the village, and the old city of Rouen
days.description:
What to expect: the garden that inspired the Water Lilies and the cathedral city Monet painted, with a licensed guide, private car, timed ticket and lunch.

Your driver collects you at your hotel at about 8:00 for the drive of about 1 hour 15 minutes down the Seine valley to Giverny. Your guide meets you for the opening of Monet's house and gardens. You start in the Clos Normand, the flower garden in front of the house, where Monet planted flowers by colour rather than by type, under arches of climbing roses and between beds that change with the seasons. Inside the pink house with green shutters, you see the studio-salon where he received visitors, the bedrooms, the bright yellow dining room and the blue-tiled kitchen, and his collection of Japanese prints, which shaped his eye.

Through a tunnel under the road you reach the Water Garden. Monet diverted a branch of the river Epte to create the pond, planted it with water lilies, bamboo, weeping willows and wisteria, and painted it obsessively for the last thirty years of his life, more than 250 times. You walk around the pond and over the green Japanese bridge as he did each day. Before lunch, you can see the Museum of Impressionisms or the village church where Monet is buried. Lunch is in the village, in a restaurant where the painters of the 'American colony' once stayed.

In the afternoon you drive to Rouen, about 50 minutes away. Its cathedral, with the tallest spire in France at 151 metres, has a façade of carved stone lace that Monet painted from a rented room opposite in 1892–1893, at every hour and in every weather. You walk through the old town of half-timbered houses, under the Gros-Horloge, a gilded Renaissance clock on an arch over the street, to the Old Market Square, where Joan of Arc was burned at the stake on 30 May 1431; a modern church shaped like an upturned boat stands on the spot. You may also see the aître Saint-Maclou, a medieval plague cemetery with carved skulls and bones. Your driver takes you back to Paris at about 17:00.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:00 – Pick-up at your hotel in Paris.
09:30 – Monet's house and the flower garden.
10:30 – The Water Garden and the Japanese bridge.
11:30 – Village of Giverny.
12:15 – Lunch.
13:30 – Drive to Rouen.
14:30 – Rouen Cathedral and the old town.
16:00 – Drive back to Paris.
17:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Monet's house and gardens are closed from November to March; in winter we offer Rouen with Honfleur or Auvers-sur-Oise, where Van Gogh lived and is buried.
• Indoors, photography is not allowed in Monet's house.
• Rouen Cathedral is closed to visitors during services.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, Monet's house and gardens ticket, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: Museum of Impressionisms, drinks with lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: When is Giverny open?
faq.answer: Monet's house and gardens are open from about 1 April to 1 November. From November to March we offer an Impressionist day in Rouen, Honfleur or Auvers-sur-Oise instead.

faq.question: When are the water lilies in flower?
faq.answer: From about June to September. Spring brings tulips, irises and wisteria on the bridge in May; autumn brings dahlias and asters. Each season is beautiful.

faq.question: Do we skip the lines?
faq.answer: We book timed tickets, so you avoid the ticket queue. The gardens are busiest from late morning; we arrive at opening time.

faq.question: Are the entrance tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes, Monet's house and gardens. Rouen Cathedral is free to enter.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, lunch in Giverny. Vegetarian, gluten-free and other diets can be arranged.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes, especially for children who like drawing; we bring sketchbooks on request. The gardens are flat and safe.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Largely. The gardens have gravel paths and the house has stairs to the upper floor. Rouen's old town is flat with some cobbles. Tell us your needs.

faq.question: Can we take photos?
faq.answer: Yes, in the gardens. Photography is not allowed inside Monet's house.

faq.question: Can we add Auvers-sur-Oise?
faq.answer: Yes, instead of Rouen. Auvers is where Van Gogh painted his last works and is buried beside his brother Theo.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes and, in spring and autumn, a light raincoat. Normandy weather changes quickly.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: May and June for the most flowers and wisteria, July and August for water lilies, September for soft light and fewer visitors.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 72 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
